newsitem.title: USA: VLSI to close wafer plant, take charge.
newsitem.headline: VLSI to close wafer plant, take charge.

text.p: Custom chip maker VLSI Technology Inc. Thursday said it plans to stop production at its San Jose wafer fabrication plant by the end of 1997, resulting in 300 job cuts and a fourth quarter charge of $100 million to $120 million.

VLSI said the San Jose plant has been underused since the company began shifting its focus in 1995. VLSI now provides semiconductor devices for cable and satellite set-top boxes, wireless communications such as cellular phones, networking equipment, computing and secure products.
"Despite the excellent performance of our San Jose (plant) and its people, the plant no longer supports our business strategies," Chairman Al Stein said.
The job cuts will take place over the next 12 months.

The company said the decision to shut the San Jose plant came only after it tried to better use or sell the plant. The company said it plans to continue looking at other options to divest the operation.
VLSI said the cutbacks will not affect its other San Jose-based operations, including headquarters, a technology development group and production test and prototype assembly facilities.
Employees whose positions are eliminated will be given 60 days notice and a competitive severance package, it said.
